verification_scope: load_completed checked source/config/checkpoint identities and complete 218-image metrics. Independently rescored all 12 saved best/final raw arrays on CPU for nine metric/count fields; every difference zero. This is not a new full-218 inference. Only best fixed-case images and the full history plot were visually reviewed here; final endpoint arrays were numerically checked, not visually compared.

nyuv2_0005.same_count: J reduces lower-wall/table depth-value error relative to L, but increases whiteboard error in places. AbsRel J 0.0543 versus L 0.0618; F1 J 0.314 versus L 0.383. The table-back edge is more often missed; the whiteboard boundary remains missed.
nyuv2_0005.J200_to_J400: AbsRel 0.0698 to 0.0543: upper-wall and table errors decrease while whiteboard error increases. F1 0.320 to 0.314, almost unchanged outlines with small losses. Not a uniform edge improvement.

nyuv2_0598.same_count: J AbsRel 0.0469 is slightly worse than L 0.0459. Large structures remain similar; table legs and sofa boundaries remain difficult. F1 J 0.446 versus L 0.550; more of the table-right edge and sofa outline is missed.
nyuv2_0598.J200_to_J400: AbsRel 0.0543 to 0.0469: tabletop/floor error is visibly lower. F1 0.416 to 0.446, with longer matched table-left boundary and some recovered right-edge fragments; still below original F1 0.537 and missing fine legs.

nyuv2_1440.same_count: J AbsRel 0.0938 improves on L 0.1061 but remains worse than B0 0.0882. Wall-value errors decrease while chair bars retain large errors. J F1 0.474 versus L 0.522, with more unmatched/missed chair slat segments; counter edge remains mostly missed.
nyuv2_1440.J200_to_J400: AbsRel 0.1066 to 0.0938, with reduced wall error. F1 0.526 to 0.474: narrow chair slats have more mismatched fragments. Clear numerical-accuracy versus fine-boundary tradeoff.

nyuv2_0226.same_count: J AbsRel 0.2115 improves on L 0.2455 and B0 0.5841, mainly in foreground table/person regions; some far-wall/column errors increase versus L. F1 0.492 versus L 0.514, with persistent branch misalignment and missed furniture edges.
nyuv2_0226.J200_to_J400: AbsRel worsens 0.1976 to 0.2115: wall, floor and portions of foreground table are brighter in the error map. F1 0.494 to 0.492, largely unchanged outlines; increased data does not fix branches or small furniture boundaries.

nyuv2_0246.same_count: J AbsRel 0.1733 is worse than L 0.1338, R 0.1269 and B0 0.1129. Broad wall/floor errors increase. F1 J 0.514 versus L 0.512 is nearly unchanged; thin stand/lamp/shelves remain missed. Retained as a failure case.
nyuv2_0246.J200_to_J400: AbsRel 0.1757 to 0.1733 is a small improvement, still clearly worse than original. Broad wall/floor errors persist. F1 0.501 to 0.514, with a slightly longer matched foreground outline, without recovering the thin stand.

nyuv2_0080.same_count: J AbsRel 0.0837 is worse than L 0.0698. Left curtain/wall error increases. F1 J 0.230 versus L 0.512: many shelf-upright matches obtained by L are absent in J; a few upper fragments survive. This is not complete edge collapse.
nyuv2_0080.J200_to_J400: AbsRel worsens 0.0758 to 0.0837, visibly in the left curtain/wall. F1 0.292 to 0.230; lower vertical shelf matches shrink while most GT boundary remains missed.

curve_review: J400 training loss continues to decline while validation fluctuates around 0.09 after its steep initial decrease. Best AbsRel is at 2200, stopping at 3200 after ten evaluations without significant improvement.

Final AbsRel is only 0.4152% above best. Nevertheless steps 2600,2800,3000,3100 exceed the 1% band and the terminal eligible suffix is too short: stable_step remains null. The predefined late_loss_down_val_up (>1% terminal degradation) flag is false; do not relabel it true.
The <=0.10 target starts at 100 and is confirmed at 300. A best below 0.09 does not establish three successive evaluations at <=0.09; that target remains unattained.
R/L columns show all three completed seeds, J shows only seed 320112, S is empty. Axes have different ranges; do not infer matched run counts or equality of curve speed from panel widths.
conclusions: J400 seed 320112 best AbsRel 0.0895224, RMSE 0.399646 m, delta1 0.924156, boundary F1 0.458373, boundary-band AbsRel 0.145971. These are single-seed observations, no seed SD.

Compared with matched J200, AbsRel decreases by 0.00439636 (about 4.68%), scene CI [-0.00841900,-0.00108592]; RMSE also improves with CI excluding zero. F1 and boundary-band differences have intervals including zero. Additional fitting data improves value accuracy without established edge-F1 improvement in this seed.

Compared with matched L400, best AbsRel improves by only 0.000531961 (about 0.59%), CI [-0.00332979,0.00221739] includes zero. F1 is lower by 0.00433078 with interval including zero. Boundary-band AbsRel improves by 0.00686989, CI [-0.01048329,-0.00383235]. Do not declare J globally superior to LoRA.

Compared with matched R400, AbsRel interval includes zero; RMSE and boundary-band error intervals favor J. F1 interval includes zero. Compared with B0, four depth-value metrics improve with conditional intervals excluding zero, but F1 interval still includes zero.

Final versus best AbsRel increases 0.4152%; RMSE improves by 0.00477738 m with interval below zero. F1 difference and boundary-band difference include zero. Retain both checkpoints and the complete curve; no metric-based reselection after seeing these secondary scores.

J has 100817 trainable parameters and peak allocated memory 4166.52 MiB. Recorded training plus validation/scoring time 2117.22 s versus matched L 759.33 s. This is run wall time under shared system conditions, not isolated GPU benchmark; cache and startup costs are recorded separately.

3200 attempted updates, 3198 successful, two recorded AMP skips, no batch/config changes. This training seed is insufficient to estimate seed variation; complete the remaining two J400 seeds and all other planned stages unchanged.
statistics_limits: One matched training seed; scene bootstrap uses 62 clusters, 2000 replicates, seed 320119, preserving image weights. These conditional intervals do not quantify initialization variation and have no multiplicity adjustment. Validation selected checkpoints; test has historical exposure. No new test evaluation here.
